cues.en: (relaxing ambient music)
cues.zh: （放鬆的環境音樂）

cues.en: Instructor: Welcome everyone to this lecture on evaluating performance, particularly for classification problems.
cues.zh: 歡迎大家，本堂介紹效能評估，尤其是分類問題。

cues.en: In the next lecture, we'll discuss evaluating performance for regression tasks.
cues.zh: 下一堂會討論迴歸任務的效能評估。

cues.en: So we just learned that after our machine learning process is complete, we're going to be using performance metrics to evaluate how our model actually did.
cues.zh: 剛學過，機器學習流程完成後，要用效能指標評估模型表現。

cues.en: And we keep mentioning the fact that we train our model on the training data and then we're gonna use some sort of metric to actually see how it performed on either the test set or the validation set.
cues.zh: 不斷提到用訓練資料訓練模型，再用某種指標查看在測試集或驗證集上的表現。

cues.en: So let's go ahead and discuss what that actually means.
cues.zh: 現在討論實際意思。

cues.en: What classification metrics are we going to be using?
cues.zh: 要用哪些分類指標？

cues.en: And the key classification metrics we should be understanding are accuracy, recall, precision and F1-score.
cues.zh: 要理解的關鍵指標是準確率、召回率、精確率與 F1 分數。

cues.en: But first, we should understand the reasoning behind these metrics and how they will actually work in the real world.
cues.zh: 不過先理解這些指標的理由，以及真實世界的運作方式。

cues.en: Typically, in any classification task, your model can actually really only achieve two results: either your model was correct in its prediction or your model was incorrect in its prediction.
cues.zh: 通常分類任務中，模型實際只有兩種結果：預測正確，或預測錯誤。

cues.en: And all classification metrics stem from this idea.
cues.zh: 所有分類指標都從這個概念而來。

cues.en: Now, fortunately, incorrect versus correct also expands the situations where you have multiple classes, such as trying to predict categories of more than two.
cues.zh: 幸好正確與錯誤也能延伸到多類別，例如預測超過兩個類別。

cues.en: For example, you have category A, B, C, D.
cues.zh: 例如有 A、B、C、D 類。

cues.en: You can either be correct in predicting the correct category or incorrect in predicting the right category.
cues.zh: 可能預測正確類別，也可能預測錯誤。

cues.en: Now for the purpose of explaining the metrics, we're gonna go ahead and simplify this to what's known as a binary classification situation, binary meaning two.
cues.zh: 為解釋指標，先簡化成二元分類，二元就是兩個。

cues.en: So there's only two available classes, either class zero or class one.
cues.zh: 所以只有類別 0 或類別 1。

cues.en: And this idea is going to expand to multiple classes as well.
cues.zh: 這個概念也會延伸至多類別。

cues.en: But for simplification, let's imagine just a binary classification situation.
cues.zh: 但為簡單起見，想像二元分類。

cues.en: So in our example, we're gonna attempt to predict if an image is a dog or a cat and we'll actually perform this task later on during the convolutional neural network portion
cues.zh: 例子是預測圖片為狗或貓。課程後面的卷積神經網路部分，

cues.en: of this course.
cues.zh: 會實際做這件事。

cues.en: Now, since it's a supervised learning problem, what we're gonna need to do first is fit or train a model on training data.
cues.zh: 因為是監督式學習，首先在訓練資料上擬合或訓練模型。

cues.en: That means we're gonna have images that someone's already gone ahead and labeled dog or cat.
cues.zh: 代表有已經被人標成狗或貓的圖片。

cues.en: So we know the correct answer on these images.
cues.zh: 所以知道圖片的正確答案。

cues.en: Then we're gonna test that model on the testing data.
cues.zh: 接著在測試資料上測試模型。

cues.en: So we're gonna show new images that the model hasn't seen before, get the model's prediction, and then compare the results of the model prediction to the correct answer that we already know.
cues.zh: 展示模型沒看過的新圖片，取得預測，再與已知的正確答案比較。

cues.en: So once we have the model's predictions from X_test data, we compare it to the true Y values, the correct labels.
cues.zh: 取得 X_test 資料的預測後，與真實 Y 值，也就是正確標籤比較。

cues.en: So let's actually diagram this process out.
cues.zh: 實際畫出流程。

cues.en: Let's imagine we've already trained our model on some training data, and now it's time to actually evaluate the model's performance.
cues.zh: 想像已用一些訓練資料訓練好模型，現在要評估效能。

cues.en: This is where our test dataset comes in.
cues.zh: 這時用測試集。

cues.en: So we take a test image from what we're gonna label X_test, X meaning features.
cues.zh: 從稱為 X_test 的資料取一張測試圖片，X 表示特徵。

cues.en: So the actual image itself is a feature and this is from the test set.
cues.zh: 實際圖片本身是特徵，來自測試集。

cues.en: And there is a corresponding correct label from y_test.
cues.zh: 另有 y_test 中對應的正確標籤。

cues.en: So we have the feature or image X, and that's the test image, and we also have the correct label from y_test.
cues.zh: 所以有特徵或圖片 X，這是測試圖片，也有 y_test 的正確標籤。

cues.en: And in this case we can see that this image is an image of a dog.
cues.zh: 這裡看到圖片是一隻狗。

cues.en: So what we're gonna do is we're just gonna feed in the features, in this case, the image into our already trained model, and then the model is going to make some prediction.
cues.zh: 只把特徵，這裡是圖片，輸入已訓練模型，讓模型預測。

cues.en: So the model predicts that this is a dog, and then what we do is we compare the prediction to the correct label.
cues.zh: 模型預測是狗，再把預測與正確標籤比較。

cues.en: So this dog equal dog, and in this case, it was correct.
cues.zh: 狗等於狗，這次正確。

cues.en: However, maybe it predicted that this image was a cat, and in this case, this comparison to the correct label would be incorrect.
cues.zh: 但也可能預測是貓，與正確標籤比較就錯了。

cues.en: And these are essentially just the only two situations.
cues.zh: 基本上只有這兩種情況。

cues.en: Either you're right or you're wrong, correct or incorrect.
cues.zh: 對或錯，正確或不正確。

cues.en: So we'll repeat this process for all the images in our X_test data, and at the end we will have a count of correct matches and a count of incorrect matches.
cues.zh: 對 X_test 所有圖片重複，最後得到正確配對數與錯誤配對數。

cues.en: And the key realization here that we need to make is that in the real world, not all incorrect or correct matches hold equal value.
cues.zh: 關鍵是要了解，在真實世界，不是所有錯誤或正確配對都同樣有價值。

cues.en: So let's kind of hone in on what we mean by that.
cues.zh: 詳細說明這個意思。

cues.en: So in the real world, a single metric won't tell the complete story.
cues.zh: 真實世界中，單一指標無法呈現全貌。

cues.en: And to understand all of this, let's bring back those four metrics we mentioned and see how they're actually calculated.
cues.zh: 帶回剛才四個指標，看看實際算法。

cues.en: We could organize our predicted values compared to the real values in what is known as a confusion matrix.
cues.zh: 可把預測值與真實值整理成所謂混淆矩陣。

cues.en: So we'll touch upon the confusion matrix later on, but first, let's talk about accuracy.
cues.zh: 稍後會談混淆矩陣，先看準確率。

cues.en: Accuracy is one of the most common classification metrics and luckily, it's also the easiest to understand.
cues.zh: 準確率是最常見的分類指標之一，幸好也最容易理解。

cues.en: It's just really intuitive what it's measuring.
cues.zh: 衡量的內容非常直覺。

cues.en: Accuracy and classification problems is the number of correct predictions made by the model, divided by the number of, or the total number of predictions.
cues.zh: 分類問題中的準確率，是模型正確預測數，除以預測總數。

cues.en: So again, it's the number of correct predictions divided by the total number of predictions, essentially answering the questions, how many predictions did you get right as a percentage?
cues.zh: 再說一次，正確預測數除以預測總數，基本上回答：預測正確的百分比是多少？

cues.en: So for example, let's imagine that X_test set was 100 images and our model correctly predicted 80 images.
cues.zh: 例如 X_test 有一百張圖片，模型預測對八十張。

cues.en: Then we have 80 divided by 100 or 0.8 or 80% accuracy.
cues.zh: 就是 80 除以 100，得到 0.8，或 80% 準確率。

cues.en: And accuracy is really useful when the target classes are well-balanced.
cues.zh: 目標類別平衡時，準確率很有用。

cues.en: So what does that mean, well-balanced?
cues.zh: 平衡是什麼意思？

cues.en: Well, in our example, that would mean we have roughly the same amount of cat images as we have dog images throughout our data.
cues.zh: 在這個例子，就是資料中貓圖片數量大致等於狗圖片數量。

cues.en: So it means the actual labels themselves are roughly equally represented in the dataset.
cues.zh: 也就是各標籤在資料集中大致同等出現。

cues.en: But let's imagine that we have what's known as an unbalanced class situation.
cues.zh: 但想像所謂類別不平衡的情況。

cues.en: In this case, accuracy is actually not a good metric to use.
cues.zh: 這時準確率就不是很好的指標。

cues.en: So let's do a little thought experiment.
cues.zh: 做個思想實驗。

cues.en: Let's imagine that in this test set we had 99 images of dogs and only 1 image of a cat.
cues.zh: 假設測試集有 99 張狗圖片，只有 1 張貓圖片。

cues.en: Now, if our model was simply a line that just always predicted dog no matter what image it saw, then we would actually get 99% accuracy on this particular test set
cues.zh: 模型如果只是一行程式，不管看到什麼永遠預測狗，在這個測試集其實能有 99% 準確率，

cues.en: because by just always saying dog, 99 images are dogs and 1 image is of a cat, then we only missed one.
cues.zh: 因為 99 張是狗、1 張是貓，永遠說狗，只錯一張。

cues.en: So that's why you have to be aware of the downside of accuracy.
cues.zh: 所以必須了解準確率的缺點。

cues.en: And the downside really comes when you have an unbalanced class situation.
cues.zh: 缺點主要發生在類別不平衡時。

cues.en: If your classes are roughly balanced, then accuracy is a very nice intuitive method or a metric to understand.
cues.zh: 類別大致平衡時，準確率是很直覺、很好理解的方法或指標。

cues.en: However, if you have an unbalanced class, you can see in this particular situation where it starts to represent a problem, and that's where the other metrics come into play.
cues.zh: 但類別不平衡時，像這個情況，就開始產生問題，這時要用其他指標。

cues.en: So again, in this situation, we'll want to understand recall and precision.
cues.zh: 所以此時要了解召回率與精確率。

cues.en: That helps us understand how well it's performing on unbalanced classes.
cues.zh: 幫助理解對不平衡類別的表現。

cues.en: Recall is the ability of a model to find all the relevant cases within a dataset.
cues.zh: 召回率是模型找出資料集中所有相關案例的能力。

cues.en: And the precise definition of recall is the number of what's known as true positives.
cues.zh: 精確定義是，所謂真陽性的數量，

cues.en: And we'll kind of hone in on that later when we see the confusion matrix, but it's the number of true positives divided by the number of true positives, plus the number of false negatives.
cues.zh: 稍後混淆矩陣會詳細介紹，就是真陽性除以真陽性加偽陰性。

cues.en: And the precision is the ability of a classification model to identify only the relevant data points where precision is defined as the number of true positives
cues.zh: 精確率是分類模型只辨識出相關資料點的能力，定義是真陽性數量

cues.en: divided by the number of true positives, plus the number of false positives.
cues.zh: 除以真陽性加偽陽性。

cues.en: Now, often, you have a trade-off between recall and precision.
cues.zh: 召回率與精確率常有取捨。

cues.en: While recall expresses the ability to find all the relevant instances in a dataset, precision expresses the proportion of the data points our model says was relevant
cues.zh: 召回率表達找出資料集中所有相關案例的能力，精確率表達模型所說的相關資料點中，

cues.en: that actually were relevant.
cues.zh: 真正相關的比例。

cues.en: And then F1-score is essentially a combination of these two.
cues.zh: F1 分數基本上結合兩者。

cues.en: In cases where we want to find an optimal blend of precision and recall, we can combine the two metrics using what is known as the F1-score.
cues.zh: 想在精確率與召回率間取得最佳平衡，可以用 F1 分數結合這兩個指標。

cues.en: And the F1-score is the harmonic mean of precision and recall, taking both metrics into account in the following equation.
cues.zh: F1 是精確率與召回率的調和平均，透過以下公式考量兩者。

cues.en: So this isn't just taking the average of recall, precision.
cues.zh: 所以不是直接取召回率與精確率的平均。

cues.en: It's taking the harmonic mean of them.
cues.zh: 是調和平均。

cues.en: And so here we have the formula for F1-score or F1-score is equal to two, times precision, times recall in the numerator, and then divided by precision, plus recall in the denominator.
cues.zh: 公式是，F1 分數的分子為 2 乘精確率乘召回率，分母為精確率加召回率。

cues.en: So the reason we use the harmonic mean instead of just a simple mean or simple average is because it's gonna punish extreme values.
cues.zh: 用調和平均而不是簡單平均，是因為它會懲罰極端值。

cues.en: For example, if you created a classifier that had a precision of one, meaning essentially perfect precision, and a recall of zero, essentially the worst recall possible,
cues.zh: 例如分類器精確率是 1，幾乎完全正確，召回率卻是 0，也就是最差召回率，

cues.en: if you were just to take the simple average of this, then it would be 0.5, but the F1-score, because it's taking a harmonic mean, we have precision times recall there at the top,
cues.zh: 直接平均會是 0.5。但 F1 用調和平均，分子有精確率乘召回率，

cues.en: which means you'd get zero times one at the top and you get an F1-score of zero.
cues.zh: 所以上面是 0 乘 1，得到 F1 等於 0。

cues.en: So this is really nice because it lets you punish extreme differences between the precision and recall.
cues.zh: 很好，能懲罰兩個指標間的極端差異。

cues.en: So it gives you kind of a fair assessment of that trade-off between precision and recall.
cues.zh: 因此對精確率與召回率的取捨有較公平的評估。

cues.en: Now we can also view all correct classified versus incorrectly classified images in the form of a confusion matrix.
cues.zh: 也能用混淆矩陣，查看所有正確與錯誤分類的圖片。

cues.en: So confusion matrix looks something like this.
cues.zh: 混淆矩陣長這樣。

cues.en: We have the underlying true conditions, so that's the true correct label.
cues.zh: 有底下真實狀態，也就是正確標籤。

cues.en: And we can think of condition as positive or negative, such as actually being a dog or not being a dog, or oftentimes is used in a medical diagnosis,
cues.zh: 狀態可想成陽性或陰性，例如實際是狗或不是狗，也常用於醫療診斷，

cues.en: such as having presence of a disease versus not having presence of a disease.
cues.zh: 例如有疾病或沒有疾病。

cues.en: And then we have the model's predicted condition.
cues.zh: 接著有模型預測的狀態。

cues.en: So prediction positive or prediction negative.
cues.zh: 預測陽性或預測陰性。

cues.en: And I think when it comes to confusion matrices, it's often easiest to first get an intuition if you think of this as a diagnostic test for having some sort of disease present in a person
cues.zh: 混淆矩陣常用疾病診斷檢驗來思考，最容易建立直覺，

cues.en: after maybe you take a blood sample and run it through your model.
cues.zh: 例如抽血後把樣本送入模型。

cues.en: So for example, a true positive would be someone actually having that disease and your model correctly predicting that they have it.
cues.zh: 真陽性是這個人真的有疾病，模型也正確預測他有。

cues.en: A true negative would be someone not having the disease and your model predicting correctly that they do not have the disease.
cues.zh: 真陰性是這個人沒有疾病，模型正確預測他沒有。

cues.en: So you have true positives and true negatives and those are both correct predictions.
cues.zh: 所以真陽性與真陰性都是正確預測。

cues.en: And then we have essentially these two types of incorrect predictions: a false positive and a false negative.
cues.zh: 接著兩種錯誤預測：偽陽性與偽陰性。

cues.en: A false positive would be if the person doesn't have the disease and you predict that they do have it.
cues.zh: 偽陽性是沒有疾病，卻預測有疾病。

cues.en: That's a false positive because you're falsely saying that they're positive for this disease or this condition.
cues.zh: 叫偽陽性，因為錯誤地說他對這個疾病或狀態呈陽性。

cues.en: A false negative is essentially the opposite of that, where this person does have the disease present and then you report back using your model on your test
cues.zh: 偽陰性則相反，這個人有疾病，但用模型或檢驗回報

cues.en: that it's actually negative, they don't actually have this disease.
cues.zh: 陰性，說他沒有這個疾病。

cues.en: And these are also sometimes called in statistics a type I error and a type II error.
cues.zh: 在統計中，也有第一類錯誤與第二類錯誤的名稱。

cues.en: And then off of these, essentially true positive true negatives, false negatives and false positives results, there's a lot of other metrics you can calculate.
cues.zh: 根據真陽性、真陰性、偽陰性、偽陽性這些結果，能計算許多其他指標。

cues.en: So we can see some of them here, such as on the bottom left corner, we can see the actual calculation for accuracy.
cues.zh: 這裡可以看到部分，例如左下角是準確率的算法。

cues.en: It's the sum of true positives plus true negatives, essentially the sum of what you got correct over the total population.
cues.zh: 真陽性加真陰性，也就是正確數量，除以總人數。

cues.en: And then there's a bunch of other ones, like positive likelihood ratio, false positive rate, true positive rate, prevalence false discovery rate, et cetera.
cues.zh: 還有正概似比、偽陽性率、真陽性率、盛行率、偽發現率等等。

cues.en: Now, the main point to remember here is that the confusion matrix and the various calculated metrics is essentially they're all fundamentally ways of comparing the predicted value versus the true values.
cues.zh: 重點是，混淆矩陣與各種計算指標，根本上都是比較預測值與真實值的方法。

cues.en: And what constitutes good metrics actually really depends on the specific situation.
cues.zh: 什麼才是好指標，真的取決於特定情境。

cues.en: A really common question I get from students is, "Hey, is this a good enough accuracy?"
cues.zh: 學生常問我：「這個準確率夠好嗎？」

cues.en: Well, that really depends on your situation and the context of the situation.
cues.zh: 真的要看情況與脈絡。

cues.en: Now, if you're still confused on the confusion matrix, it's no problem, check out the Wikipedia page for it.
cues.zh: 如果仍不懂混淆矩陣，沒關係，可以看維基百科頁面。

cues.en: It has a really good diagram with all the formulas for all the metrics.
cues.zh: 有很好圖解，以及所有指標公式。

cues.en: And throughout the training in this course, we're usually just gonna print out metrics, such as printing out basic accuracy.
cues.zh: 本課訓練時，通常只會印出指標，例如基本準確率。

cues.en: Now, before we finish off this lecture, I wanna go back to that initial question I mentioned that students ask me all the time, which is this idea of "What is a good enough accuracy?"
cues.zh: 結束前，再回到學生常問的最初問題：「怎樣的準確率才夠好？」

cues.en: And as always, this really depends on the context of the situation you're running your model in.
cues.zh: 一樣，要看執行模型的情境。

cues.en: There's no single number I can give to say something like 90% accuracy is good enough for every situation.
cues.zh: 沒有單一數字，不能說 90% 對所有情況都夠好。

cues.en: We already saw the issue with unbalanced classes, but there's also not really a good remark I can give for what is a good enough precision or recall.
cues.zh: 已看過類別不平衡問題，也沒有通用說法能判斷精確率或召回率多好才夠。

cues.en: And we have to think of the context of the situation.
cues.zh: 必須考慮情境。

cues.en: So let's think back on maybe that model that is diagnostic for predicting the presence of a disease.
cues.zh: 回想預測疾病的診斷模型。

cues.en: So if we created a model to predict the presence of a disease, first thing we wanna think about is, are we gonna have balanced classes or unbalanced classes?
cues.zh: 建立模型預測疾病，先想類別平衡還是不平衡？

cues.en: So is the disease presence well balanced in the general population?
cues.zh: 這種疾病在一般人口中的分布平衡嗎？

cues.en: And in pretty much most cases, it's probably not.
cues.zh: 大部分情況，可能不會。

cues.en: There's probably not a disease that's gonna happen where about half the population is affected and half the population is not affected.
cues.zh: 不太可能有一半人口患病、另一半沒患病。

cues.en: So we can already tell we're gonna have an unbalanced class situation, which means we're gonna have a precision/recall trade-off.
cues.zh: 所以已能看出會有類別不平衡，也就是精確率與召回率的取捨。

cues.en: So we should also keep in mind that often these models are used as quick diagnostic tests to have before having a more invasive test.
cues.zh: 還要記得，這些模型常用作快速診斷，在更侵入的檢查前先做。

cues.en: For example, for prostate cancer models, it's really common to just do a simple urine test before getting a biopsy because it's much easier
cues.zh: 例如前列腺癌模型，通常先做簡單尿液檢驗，再做切片，因為

cues.en: to just get your urine tested than going through a full biopsy on the prostate.
cues.zh: 驗尿比完整前列腺切片容易得多。

cues.en: So we also need to consider then what is at stake.
cues.zh: 所以還得考量後果。

cues.en: If it's prostate cancer, the stakes are actually quite high.
cues.zh: 若是前列腺癌，後果相當重大。

cues.en: So as we mentioned, we often have that precision/recall trade-off, which means we essentially need to decide if the model should focus on fixing false positives versus false negatives.
cues.zh: 如剛才說的，常有精確率／召回率取捨，基本上要決定模型應優先減少偽陽性還是偽陰性。

cues.en: So at the cost of decreasing false negatives, most likely we increase false positives and vice versa.
cues.zh: 減少偽陰性時，很可能增加偽陽性，反之亦然。

cues.en: And in disease diagnosis, it's probably better to try to minimize the number of false negatives at the cost of increasing the number of false positives.
cues.zh: 疾病診斷時，通常寧可增加偽陽性，也要盡量減少偽陰性。

cues.en: So we go in the direction of these false positives, and why do we actually wanna do that?
cues.zh: 所以往容許偽陽性的方向移，為什麼？

cues.en: Well, we wanna make sure we correctly classify as many cases of the disease as possible.
cues.zh: 因為要確保盡可能正確找出所有患病案例。

cues.en: So at the cost of increasing false positives, we try our best to decrease false negatives in this context of disease diagnosis.
cues.zh: 所以疾病診斷這種情境，寧可增加偽陽性，也要盡力降低偽陰性。

cues.en: And why would we actually wanna do that?
cues.zh: 為什麼要這樣？

cues.en: Well, we wanna make sure that anyone that actually has some sort of presence of this disease or in this case of this example, prostate cancer, if we're doing that urine test,
cues.zh: 因為要確保任何真的有這個疾病，這裡例如前列腺癌的人，做尿液檢驗時，

cues.en: we wanna make sure that all those people that have the presence of the disease will actually go through to the next step that is maybe a more invasive test, like a biopsy.
cues.zh: 所有患病者都能進入下一步，可能是更侵入的檢查，例如切片。

cues.en: And remember, this kind of usually comes at a cost of increasing those false positives.
cues.zh: 記得，通常代價是偽陽性增加。

cues.en: So our models aren't gonna be perfect.
cues.zh: 所以模型不完美。

cues.en: And eventually what's gonna happen is someone who doesn't have the disease, when we do our simple urine test or whatever our machine learning model is, it's gonna predict back that, Hey, I'm sorry,
cues.zh: 最後可能出現沒有疾病的人，用簡單驗尿或其他機器學習模型時，預測回報「很抱歉，

cues.en: but you have the positive presence of this disease, and it'll be an error because it'll be a false positive.
cues.zh: 你對這個疾病呈陽性」，這會是偽陽性錯誤。

cues.en: However, then when they get the more invasive test, then they'll realize, oh, sorry, it was a false positive.
cues.zh: 不過做更侵入檢查後，就會發現剛才是偽陽性。

cues.en: You're actually okay. You don't have this disease.
cues.zh: 其實沒事，沒有這個疾病。

cues.en: And that comes because we're trying to minimize the false negatives, What we really don't want when it comes as something as important as having cancer, having a disease,
cues.zh: 因為我們盡量降低偽陰性。像癌症或疾病這麼重要的事，

cues.en: we really don't want to turn someone away who actually has a disease and tell 'em they don't have the disease.
cues.zh: 不希望把真的有疾病的人送走，卻說他沒有病。

cues.en: So that would be a false negative.
cues.zh: 那就是偽陰性。

cues.en: When it comes to disease diagnosis, that's something we really want to minimize.
cues.zh: 疾病診斷時，這是很想避免的。

cues.en: We wanna minimize those false negatives so we don't accidentally miss someone right off the bat with our diagnostic tool and tell 'em, "Oh, you don't have the disease" or "you don't have cancer"
cues.zh: 要盡量降低偽陰性，避免診斷工具一開始就漏掉病人，對他說「你沒病」或「你沒有癌症」，

cues.en: when they actually do have it.
cues.zh: 但實際有。

cues.en: So we can see, for something as important as disease diagnosis, really, minimizing those false negatives becomes really important.
cues.zh: 所以像疾病診斷這種重要事，降低偽陰性就很重要。

cues.en: And pretty much all of this is to say machine learning is not gonna be performed in a vacuum and these performance metrics don't have some sort
cues.zh: 這一切表示，機器學習不會在真空中進行，效能指標也沒有某種

cues.en: of universal truth that is true across all problems.
cues.zh: 適用所有問題的普遍真理。

cues.en: But machine learning is, instead, it's a really collaborative process where we should always be consulting with experts in the domain.
cues.zh: 機器學習其實是協作過程，應始終諮詢領域專家。

cues.en: For example, in this case of disease diagnosis, we should probably be talking to medical doctors as far as what are acceptable standards for false negatives versus false positives,
cues.zh: 例如疾病診斷，應詢問醫師，偽陰性與偽陽性的可接受標準，

cues.en: what is the general presence of this disease in the general population, et cetera.
cues.zh: 以及疾病在一般人口的盛行情況等等。

cues.en: And this is going to change depending on the context of your situation.
cues.zh: 這會隨情境而改變。

cues.en: So always keep that in mind.
cues.zh: 所以永遠記得。

cues.en: There's not gonna be an easy answer for me to say, is this a good enough accuracy, precision, or recall, because it all depends on the context and the domain of the situation, okay.
cues.zh: 沒有簡單答案能說準確率、精確率或召回率是否夠好，因為全都取決於情境與領域，好嗎？

cues.en: So we just talked about how we can evaluate classification models.
cues.zh: 剛談完分類模型的評估。

cues.en: Let's go ahead and move on to the next lecture where we discuss evaluating regression tasks.
cues.zh: 下一堂討論迴歸任務的評估。

cues.en: I'll see you there.
cues.zh: 到時見。
